what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: Jammed clusters of records: what moves, what is frozen, how they grow and evaporate. SETTING (the owner's working reading, 2026-09-20; block 39, the open PR titled 'ail39: records that move'): a site is empty or carries ONE record; a record carries its content (six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega, omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal axes; a bond with an empty end weighs 1; the axioms' rule K (normalized over contents) does not depend on the scale c. MOTION: a record chooses between its position and an empty neighbouring position in proportion to the pair weights it would have there; this is in detailed balance with the static law on the occupied set. The neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r): an empty neighbour weighs what a record of random content weighs on average, and it is the least scale at which the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes. Simulator: probes/lib/moving_gas.py p q r scale rho L sweeps seed (scale = a number or the word neutral). The owner's remark: a region does not have to be very full to jam, and a jammed region is where nothing can happen any more. Under pair-weight transit a record with k agreeing neighbours leaves with probability 1/(1 + (c p)^k), and a record with no empty neighbour cannot move at all. TASK: for a convex cluster of aligned records in empty space, with rare formation at rate z Z_x: (a) which records can ever move (the surface), and how the number of arrangements reachable in a time T scales with the cluster's volume and with its surface; (b) the growth law of the cluster by sticking and by formation at its surface, and its evaporation rate, as functions of its size; is there a size above which a cluster only grows? (c) whether contents inside are frozen forever, and what an observer who can read only records (the axioms: only records are readable) can learn about the interior from the surface. State theorems for finite clusters with exact small checks; no identification with anything in nature is asked for. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/moving-jammed-clusters/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/moving-jammed-clusters/<name>/check.py"
